title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during smartphone interaction
description: This dataset comprises multimodal physiological recordings from 23 healthy adult participants collected during naturalistic smartphone interaction and standardized video viewing conditions. Simultaneous EEG (64-channel), eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) data were acquired, synchronized via hardware TTL pulses. The dataset supports research into physiological and neural correlates of smartphone use and passive video viewing.
methods_description: Participants wore a 64-channel EEG cap and head-mounted eye tracker while simultaneous PPG and GSR were recorded. Two conditions were tested: a 10-minute naturalistic smartphone interaction task and a 5-minute standardized video viewing task. Hardware TTL synchronization pulses (five pulses at ~1-second intervals for session boundaries, additional pulses every 20 seconds) were embedded in EEG and eye-tracking streams for cross-modal temporal alignment. EEG event markers denoted condition onset/offset (S12/S13 for Smartphone Monitor, S22/S23 for Video Monitor).
